newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM says lira loss to stay below inflation.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM says lira loss to stay below inflation.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said the lira's depreciation rate would remain below the inflation rate.
"There will not be any lira depreciation above inflation. No one should run towards foreign currencies," Erbakan told a joint news conference with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller in Ankara.
Ciller said those who invest in foreign currency would lose.
"No one should be deceived. We don't want anybody to make loss. We are trying to make it clear that any rise in (the lira depreciation) above inflation should not be expected," she said.
Turkey has been keeping the lira depreciation rate below inflation since early 1994 as part of its monetary policy, which aimed at curbing high inflation.

The lira's depreciation rate against the dollar was around 41 percent since the beginning of 1996 after a 35-percent depreciation in all of 1995, down from annual 1995 wholesale inflation of 65.6 percent.
